facts: The appeal is directed against the judgment dated 01.09.2010 of the Delhi High Court in Criminal Appeal No.232 of 1997 filed by the appellant-Suresh Singhal against his conviction and the sentence awarded to him.
The incident occurred on the 04.03.1991 at about 5:15 pm.
The deceased-Shyam Sunder and Kishan Lal, both brothers, were killed in the incident at the office of Lala Harkishan Dass located at Rajendra Park, Nangloi.
The statement of Lala Harkishan Dass was recorded.
issues: Whether there was a scuffle or not determines the tenability of the main submission advanced by Mr. Sushil Kumar, the learned senior counsel, that the appellant acted in the exercise of his right of private defence and shot the deceased.
The stark difference between the two versions is that of the scuffle preceding the incident of the shooting.
petitioner_arguments: The main submission advanced by Mr. Sushil Kumar, the learned senior counsel, that the appellant acted in the exercise of his right of private defence and shot the deceased.
court_reasoning: In fact a scuffle did take place.
Shyam Sunder alone, or along with his two brothers tried to strangulate the appellant-Suresh Singhal.
The shot in question was obviously not a close shot.
There is another reason which lends credence to the assumption that the shot was not fired from close quarters, and that is the fact that the bullet did not exit the body.
holding: Culpable homicide is not murder if it is committed without premeditation in a sudden fight in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel and without the offender's having taken undue advantage or acted in a cruel or unusual manner.
The appellant killed the deceased in the exercise of the right of private defence.
The conviction of the appellant - Suresh Singhal under section 302 IPC for murder of Kishan Lal is set aside and his conviction under section 304 IPC is maintained.
